Maren gives you the answer slowly, a few steps at a time, as if each memory had to be taken down from a high shelf.

Your mother, she says, was a hoarder of flat river stones. As a girl she chalked maps of the Deepwatch's corridors on them and left them in odd corners, so that for years the wardens found little grey stones in the lamp-niches with a corridor drawn on them and a tiny, furious arrow. She loved barley-and-honey cakes and sour plum jam, and could not be kept from the kitchens. She sang one song, badly and loudly, a lamp-maker's work-song called "Seven Wicks," and every warden on the seventh gallery knew it by heart whether they wanted to or not. She would not wear a helm in the shafts until she cracked her head on a low lintel at twelve, and after that she wore one for the rest of her life and complained about it daily.

Maren hums a bar of the song under her breath, flat and dry, and you realize with a start that you know the tune. Father Dorrin used to whistle it while he mended the shrine roof.

She tells you of the Deepwatch too: a hall cut into a single mountain, seven galleries high, with a lamp-lit Hall of Names where every warden's death is carved. A few dozen wardens and their kin still live there, and it has grown very quiet since the holds fell. Its captain is a stern dwarf named Torvald Greycairn, who was Maren's rival for forty years and is, she admits, probably her only friend. He disapproved of your mother's marriage, she adds, and she lets that sit.

By evening the waymark-hut stands at the saddle, a low stone shelter with a turf roof and a hearth and a stack of dry peat left by some earlier traveler. Garrick has already checked the corners, and he nods once. You keep your promise and cook: oatcakes toasted on the hearthstone, dried apple stewed in a pot, a bit of cheese. Maren eats two helpings and says the stew is not bad for a priest.

It is a little past six. The wind is rising off the hills, the hut is warm, and the Deepwatch lies a day and a half north. You have three spell slots and Channel Divinity. What does Brun do?

Brun sits back by the peat fire with her bowl and hums a flat, loud bar of "Seven Wicks," then grins at Maren. "Father Dorrin whistled that every time he mended the roof, and I never knew it was hers. Will you teach me the words tonight?"

She adds, "Garrick, would you take the first watch and wake me for the second? And Aunt Maren, you said Torvald Greycairn disapproved of my mother's marriage, so when you're ready, I'd like to hear a little about my father too."

Maren puts down her bowl and clears her throat like a woman about to be paid for something she'd rather do for free. Then she sings it. Her voice is cracked and thin and entirely without shame, and the old song comes out in a plain, rolling rhythm about a lamp-maker's daughter and seven wicks, each one lit for a thing she had lost. By the third verse you have the tune, and by the fifth you are singing it loud and flat, exactly as Sigrun did. Garrick, on watch at the door, does not turn his head, but his shoulders shake once.

When the song is done and the fire has burned low, you ask about your father, and she is quiet a long while.

"I will give you a little," she says, "and the rest at the Deepwatch, where it is written in stone as he deserves. He was a lamp-maker from a hill-hold, a quiet dwarf with soot in the creases of his hands and eyes as dark as yours. He made the lamps for the seventh gallery, the ones that never smoke. That is why she wrote his trade into the song, and why every corner of the seventh gallery has a lamp in it that she insisted on." She almost smiles. "Torvald objected because he would not swear the wardens' oath. He said he was a lamp-maker and not a soldier, and that he would light the way for anyone but would not choose a side. It was the stubbornest thing I ever heard from a man who weighed nothing. They married anyway."

She pats your hand. "His name is carved. You will read it there."

Garrick takes the first watch and wakes you for the second. Nothing stirs in the hills but the wind. The night passes, and the grey dawn finds you at the doorway of the hut with the whole high country laid out before you, cold and pale and clean.

It is just before six on day six. You are at 21 of 21 with all spell slots and Channel Divinity. The Deepwatch lies a day or less ahead, and Garrick says the weather is turning. A bank of cloud is building in the north.

What does Brun do?

Brun studies the building clouds and turns to Garrick. "You know these hills better than I do. Do we push on and try to reach the Deepwatch before the weather breaks, or find shelter along the way? I'll follow your read."

She helps Maren to her feet and tucks Ilsa's wool scarf around her aunt's shoulders. "Aunt Maren, if the wind gets bad, take my arm and keep the scarf up, and tell me the moment you tire."

Garrick studies the north for a long minute, wets a finger, and watches the cloud-bank crawl. "It will break by dusk," he says. "Hard. But the Deepwatch is a long day off, not two, and the track runs along the lee of the ridge the whole way. We push. Slow and steady, no stops but short ones, and the old woman rides my pack-strap at the steep places." Maren snorts at that, but she does not argue.

It is a long, hard day. The wind rises through the morning and by noon it is a living thing, tugging at your cloak and plucking at the scarf you have tied about Maren's shoulders. You walk at her side with her arm through yours, and twice she leans on you more than she means to, and you say nothing. The first cold drops of rain come at three, and by four the sky has gone the color of slate. Garrick's route holds: every time the weather seems about to catch you, the track bends in under a shoulder of rock and the worst of it goes by overhead.

A little before half past five, in the first real roar of the storm, you come over the last rise and the Deepwatch stands before you.

It is a single mountain with a face cut into it. Seven rows of narrow, lamplit windows climb the cliff like a stair of gold, and below them, set deep under a great overhanging brow of stone, stand a pair of bronze-banded doors twice the height of a dwarf. A lamp burns on either side of them, steady against the wind. On the wall above, a sentry in a hooded warden's cloak has already spotted you and leans over the parapet with a lantern.

"Who comes to the Deepwatch in the storm?" the sentry calls in Dwarvish. "Maren? Is that you? Gods, you are three days late. And who is that with you, the one with the dented mail?"

Maren straightens beneath your hand and lifts her chin, and in the rain her face is suddenly very proud.

"Tell the captain," she says, and her voice carries, "that Sigrun's daughter has come home."

You are at 21 of 21, with three spell slots and Channel Divinity, in the shelter of the gate. What does Brun do?

Brun squares her shoulders, wipes the rain from her face, and calls up to the sentry in clear Dwarvish, "I'm Brunhilde Stonehearth, Sigrun's daughter, raised by Father Dorrin Ashbeard. I carry a copy of the Hearthdeep warden-captain's ledger, and I've come home."

She keeps one hand on Maren's arm and glances at Garrick. "Stay close, friend. You're with me, and you're welcome here."

time: 1 hour later: Day 6, 6:29:30 PM

Your voice carries over the wind and the rain, clear and unhurried, in the old tongue. For a moment the sentry stares. Then he is gone from the parapet, and you hear the sound of bolts drawn back inside the stone.

The great doors open on a gate hall of dressed granite, its roof lost in lamplight and its floor worn smooth by a thousand years of boots. A dozen wardens in grey and hammer-brooched cloaks stand along the walls, still as pillars, and at the far end under a stern carved arch a single dwarf waits: iron-bearded, heavy-browed, his cloak pinned with a captain's seven-lamp brooch. Torvald Greycairn. He says nothing at all while you cross the hall, until Maren steps forward and lays her palm flat on his chest.

"You old fool," she says. "I told you I'd find her."

His jaw works. He looks at her hand, and then at you, and then at the ring on your finger, and his face does something very difficult to put a name to. "Aye," he says, gruff and hoarse. "You did."

You offer the ledger, and he takes it in both hands as if it were warm. He opens it to the faded blue ribbon and reads the captain's last leaf, and his lips move over the Naming. When he looks up his eyes are bright. "The Naming," he says. "It was lost with the holds. We have waited forty years for this." He closes it. "It will be copied tonight and set in the archive with Corm's name on it, and yours. You have done the Deepwatch a service we cannot repay, daughter of Sigrun."

He does not embrace you, because he is not that sort of dwarf. But he lays one hard hand on your shoulder and says, "The Hall of Names is closed at night. At first light I will take you there myself. There is a page you should read."

A warden brings you hot broth, a clean bed in the guest gallery, and a dry cloak. Garrick, silent as ever, is shown to a bunk beside yours and sleeps with his bow within reach. Maren is already sleeping in a chair by the fire, wrapped in your scarf.

It is half past six. Your spells are full. The Hall of Names waits for morning.

What does Brun do?

Brun thanks the warden for the broth and the cloak, then turns to Torvald and bows her head. "Thank you, Captain Greycairn. I'll be at the Hall of Names at first light, and I'd be honored if Aunt Maren and Garrick could come with me."

She tucks the blanket more snugly around Maren in her chair, then sits by the fire with Father Dorrin's prayer book and softly says the evening prayers, adding her mother's name and her father's, though she doesn't yet know it, before she lies down to sleep.

You say the evening prayers by the fire and add two names, your mother's and a second you do not yet have. In the gap where it belongs you say only, "my father," and the fire pops softly as if in answer. Then you sleep, deeply, in a bed that smells of clean wool and lamp-oil.

Before first light a warden raps on the door. Torvald is waiting in the corridor with a lantern, Maren leaning on her staff beside him, and Garrick already dressed and silent behind you. The captain leads you down, gallery after gallery, past lamp-niches each holding a small flat river stone with a corridor chalked on it. You notice them now. At the lowest level a plain oak door opens on the Hall of Names.

It is a long, quiet chamber with a vault like an upturned boat, lit by a single row of lamps whose flames do not flicker or smoke. Every wall is carved: names, hundreds of them, row on row, and beneath each the date and a hammer-and-three-lines mark. Torvald lifts his lantern and walks you to the far end, the seventh gallery's wall, and stops.

There, among the wardens, is your mother's name: SIGRUN STONEHEARTH, SURVEYOR. And beneath it, cut a little deeper and a little more carefully than the rest, is another.

DAGRIM WICKWRIGHT, LAMP-MAKER. HE WOULD NOT SWEAR. HE DUG.

"He dug for three days beside my wardens," Torvald says, low and gravelly. "A man who weighed nothing and would not choose a side. When the second fall came he was pulling the last timber from over the place where the child lay. It took him. I had his name cut myself, the week after, among the wardens, though he never swore." His jaw works. "I was wrong about him. I have been wrong about him for forty years. Dorrin found you on the fourth day, under your mother, with his lamp lying beside you, still lit."

You put your hand on the stone. It is cool, and the carving is clean-edged. Maren's hand finds your shoulder.

After a long time Torvald clears his throat. "The Deepwatch has a place for a priest of the Morninglord, if you want one. But there is another matter. Hearthdeep was not the only hold the wardens sealed. Four more seals are named in our archive, their keepers long dead. With the Naming copied and your example, a priest could mend them, or release what sleeps there with mercy. I would not ask you to carry it. I ask you to think on it."

The lamps burn steady on the wall. You are at 21 of 21, with 700 of the 900 XP for third level, and a ring on your finger. What does Brun do?

Brun keeps her hand on her father's name a long moment, then traces the words *he would not swear, he dug* with her thumb. "Thank you, Captain. Thank you for cutting it, and for telling me true."

She turns, wipes her eyes, and says, "I'll think on the four seals, and I'll not say no. But first I'd like to sit here a while with my mother and father, and say the morning prayers aloud with Aunt Maren. DM: remind me, which of Father Dorrin's last words did I never get to read, and is there anything more in the back of his book I haven't checked?"

Torvald steps back without a word and takes his lantern with him as far as the door, and Garrick goes with him, closing it softly. You and Maren are left in the long hush of the hall, with the single row of steady lamps and your parents' names above your head.

You say the morning prayers aloud, Father Dorrin's cramped phrases in your low voice and Maren's dry one beneath it. At the end you say both names, slowly, once each. When the last word is spoken the room is quiet in a way that feels like being listened to.

You answer your own question as you close the book. You have read three leaves in its back pages, but you have never read the leather of the back cover itself. Your thumb catches on a stiffness there, a ridge you took for old stitching. You work your nail under it and a single folded leaf slides out, pressed flat, soft as cloth with age, written in the cramped hand you know best of anything in the world.

*Brun,*

*If you read this, you have found your people, and I am glad past saying. I kept this book for you because it is all of me I could give you that would not rot.*

*I wrote three letters to the Deepwatch in your first year, asking them to come for you. I never had an answer. I told myself it was grief that kept them away. I have not been sure since. The props in that shaft were cut, child. I saw the ends when we dug. I have never known by whom, and I was too afraid for you to say so aloud.*

*Forgive an old man his silence. The Morninglord found you in the dark through me. I would not trade it. Walk in the light and do not be afraid of the dark places; you are made of them.*

*Dorrin.*

You read it twice. Then you read it aloud to Maren, because she will want to hear it from your mouth, and when you reach the part about the letters her whole body goes still.

"Three," she says. "Dorrin wrote three? We had one. One only. It said she was safe, that she was with a priest, and that she should not be sought, that warden's blood on the road would bring harm to her." Her voice is flat and very quiet. "We were told this was Dorrin's wish. We believed it was." She looks at the carved names on the wall, and then at you, and there is something very old and very hard in her face. "Someone has kept us apart for forty years, Brunhilde."

The lamps burn steady. Somewhere above you a bell rings the hour. You are at 21 of 21, with a leaf in your hand, a ring on your finger, and two things on your road now: four sealed holds that Torvald has asked you to consider, and a hand that cut a shaft's props, which has not yet been named.

Torvald is waiting outside the door with his lantern. He listens to you without interrupting, and when you reach the part about the third letter his jaw sets like a latch. "Three," he says. "I will not call it a lie until I see it. Come."

He takes the three of you up to the archive on the fourth gallery, a low room of pigeonholes and oak chests that smells of dust and cold lamp-oil. From a locked drawer he lifts a single folded sheet, brittle at the creases, and lays it on the table under the steady lamps.

You set it beside the cramped, leaning script of the leaf in your prayer book. To your eye they are not the same. Garrick takes his place at the top of the last stair with his bow unstrung, eyes on the corridor, and says nothing. You go on with Torvald and Maren, past lamp-niches each holding a small grey stone with a corridor chalked on it.

Osric Vane's cell is a bare stone room with a cot, a stool and a shelf of dry inkwells. The old Keeper sits by a cold brazier in a blanket, small as a child, his eyes milky and bright. At first he calls Torvald "Haldor" and asks if the post has come. Maren kneels and tells him her name, and something clears in his face like a lamp being trimmed.

"Maren Stonehearth," he says. "Aye. You came asking for the little one. Every week you came." He turns his head toward you, though he cannot see you well. "Her chin. Sigrun's chin."

Then he tells it, slowly, as if setting down a load. Kell Marrow, the seal-bearer, brought him a priest's letters already opened and told him to burn them and write one soft reply in a clerk's hand, "by the captain's word." Osric was Keeper and it was not his place to ask. But he could not burn a priest's letters. "A man who asks for a child in the dark," he says. "I could not."

As he speaks you watch Torvald and not the old man. The captain's face goes grey, not guarded. It is the look of a man hearing his own house described by a stranger. You are as sure as you can be that he did not know.

"The captain then," Torvald says, barely audible. "Say it, Osric."

"Haldor," the old man whispers. "Your father, boy. I am sorry. I am so sorry."

Osric points a shaking finger at the lamp-niche nearest the door. Under a grey river stone, with a corridor chalked on it in a furious small hand and a tiny arrow, is a hollow in the wall. In it lie two letters in Father Dorrin's leaning script, their seals broken and folded again with care, and softened by forty years of dry air. You take them. Maren says the stone is Sigrun's.

Torvald stands very still, his hand over the seven-lamp brooch at his breast. "My father," he says. "Whatever he did, I will have the whole of it, and so will you. I give you my word before the Deepwatch." He does not say what he will do if the answer is bad.

It is a little after eight. Kell Marrow is dead. Osric is spent and should rest. The letters are in your hand, unread, and there is still the question of who cut the props and why Haldor wanted a child kept hidden. What does Brun do?

description.text: A squat stone inn with a shrine lean-to on a mountain road, rain-soaked. A fresh rockslide has buried part of the road beyond it, trapping a wagon of travelers (wounded merchant, child, mule-driver).
Late priest of the Morninglord who found Brun as a starving orphan in a collapsed mine shaft and raised her in his small shrine. Brun carries his prayer book.

Free the trapped wagon party (wounded merchant, child, mule-driver) from beneath the fresh rockslide without bringing the slope down again. Locals argue over whether to dig: nervous caravan guard, sullen hunter, innkeeper.
Brun rallied the guard and hunter (Persuasion 18). Hunter will share what he knows of the slope. Trapped party answers by tapping.

Trapped: merchant Ilsa (crushed leg, drifting unconscious), mule-driver Tam, child Pip. Brun is digging from the left (solid ledge by old cairn), top stones first, with planks bracing; hunter watching slope. Survival 17 read the rubble well; about 30 minutes in, an opening is near.

Pip freed and safe with the guard. Brun healed Ilsa with Healing Word (7 HP) and levered the rack with Tam (Athletics 16 with help); Ilsa dragged clear, leg still badly hurt and needs further care. Slope held.

Medicine check failed (7): Brun's first splint was off; Ilsa's shin bone is displaced and the set won't hold without a second attempt or magic. Ilsa lies in the inn's warmest room. Hunter and Tam tending the mule. Ilsa has something to say about her cargo (hook).
Second attempt succeeded (Medicine 18): bone reset cleanly and Cure Wounds (10 HP) eased Ilsa; she sleeps. Brun has no spell slots left until a long rest. Ilsa wanted a word about her cargo.

Day 2 ~9 AM: Brun promised Hild Ironvein to help bring her kin out of sealed Hearthdeep once the foul air from the Iron-Banded Door is understood. Garrick takes the sick (Aldric, Dunna, the boy) to the waystation on a cart. Brun's spells won't return until another long rest (earliest ends Day 3, 4 AM). The slide itself was caused from above/by something, not by Hild's crew.
Noon Day 2: Garrick returns with food and word that Ilsa is awake and insists on speaking to Brun alone; she says her cargo is not what her manifest says.

Ilsa told Brun of the Lead-Lined Chest (see item): a grey-bearded, scar-forearmed dwarf paid her triple to leave it at the old cairn. It is still in the wagon wreck at the road. Ilsa fears it caused the slide.

Night Day 2: Brun, Corm, Garrick, Tam and the guard lifted the chest on planks wrapped in wet canvas and carried it uphill to the tunnel (Athletics 12 success, Survival 9: lost the path briefly, plank slipped, Brun took 2 damage). They reach the tunnel mouth around 9 PM with Hild waiting.
Resolved: all three trapped travelers saved; chest returned to the door; Hild's crew sworn not to open it. Remaining thread: the half-mended seal and Hearthdeep's dead.

Garrick Thorne says that for two weeks he has seen lantern light high on the slope at night and found fresh spoil and cut timber near the old cairn: someone has been tunneling, and the rockslide may not have been natural. He will show Brun at first light.

Garrick says the cut timber is fine, square-sawn work, not rough human hacking; the beams were cut to a measured length, which is dwarf-style or someone who learned it. Only Garrick and the occasional goatherd use the old cairn path; nobody honest has reason to be there at night.

Day 2 morning: Garrick led Brun to the old cairn. Tunnel mouth found behind a stack of loose rock, timbered with square-sawn props. Brun failed Perception (5) on the climb and did not notice a watcher on the ledge above, who has seen them and slipped inside.
Sullen hunter who knows the slope above the waystation. Taciturn and gruff, but softened by Brun's competence. Suspects someone has been digging on the slope and offers to show Brun at first light.
Day 4 ~1 PM: Garrick joins Brun as a companion for the road north to the Deepwatch. Human ranger 2 (Archery), mountain terrain, favored enemy monstrosities; knows the high passes.

A burned-in maker's brand (a hammer over three wavy lines) on the tunnel timbers and the broken pick's haft, the mark of the old mine-wardens of Hearthdeep, the hill-hold near the shaft where Brun was found as a child. The mark is old, though the wood is fresh-cut, meaning the diggers hold stock or tools stolen from, or taken from, the old warden stores.

Gruff dwarf woman, leader of a small band digging into the old Hearthdeep galleries from the slope. Speaks Dwarvish, wary, has a crossbow trained on the tunnel mouth. Her motives are not yet known; she did not want the slope to fall.

Persuasion 12 (just short): Hild half-trusts Brun. Knew Father Dorrin's name ("the old Ashbeard") but not enough to trust. She'll let Brun alone in to see her sick comrade, but only if Brun leaves her warhammer at the mouth and Garrick stays out. She insists her crew did not bring the slope down.

Crew: Aldric (hurt), Dunna (one-eyed woman, coughing), and a young man with a pick (also coughing). Motive revealed after Brun moved everyone out: the lower Hearthdeep galleries were sealed after a collapse about forty winters ago that trapped many of the hold's dead; Hild's kin among them. The crew dug in to bring them out for proper burial. The warden stores and timber were taken from the sealed upper stores.

Night Day 2: Persuasion 17: Hild heard Corm's confession and gave Brun her word that nobody opens the door until the stone is set back and the thing behind it understood. She grieves: her brother is one of the sixty. She wants him honored, not freed.
Injured dwarf in Hild Ironvein's crew, hurt when the seam gave way; has a wet, ragged cough and is lying on a pallet in a side gallery of the tunnel.

Brun's Medicine check 11 (just short) and Cure Wounds (7 HP): his crushed ribs knit somewhat and his color improved, but the wet cough persists. Brun suspects it is not only the ribs. Hild says he was hurt when the seam gave way a day ago; his cough began before that, after the crew got near the iron-banded door.

Day 3 afternoon: Brun (Medicine 23) found Aldric, Dunna and the young miner (Tobin) all recovering in clean air at the waystation; cough fading, no lasting damage. Ilsa's leg is mending and she means to be on the road in a week. Garrick and the innkeeper promised to keep the cairn path closed.

A great iron-banded door of old dwarf stone half-cleared of clay at the end of the tunnel gallery. Cold, foul-smelling air seeps from the seams. The crew's coughs started after they got close to it. Likely a sealed gate into the lower mines of Hearthdeep.

Day 2: Brun studied Hild's charcoal rubbing of the door marks (History/Stonecunning 11, short of DC 13): confirmed warden work from about forty winters ago, a deliberate seal, with a repeated three-stroke sign she could not read; it could mean 'bury' or 'keep shut'. Hild's half-map of the lower galleries shows a gallery marked with a sign like a hammer split in two. Corm may know the marks.

Seal explained by Corm: the three-stroke sign means 'bound, not buried'. The lower galleries did not simply collapse; the wardens sealed something living and sleeping behind it, and a heartstone set in the door held it. Without the stone the seal weakens.

Night Day 2 ~10 PM: the heartstone was carried in and set back into the door. Brun's WIS save held; her binding prayer (Religion 10) was not enough to fully reseat it. The stone sits, the hum quiets to a low sleeper's breath, but the seal is only half-mended and needs a warden to keep it and a true rite of binding. Corm chose to stay as its keeper, as his master did; Hild stays with him.

Lean, grey-bearded dwarf in Hild's crew who keeps the camp fire. Silent, watchful, and was a warden's apprentice at Hearthdeep as a boy; he knows the sealing marks better than he admits and is reluctant to speak of them.

Persuasion 7 failed: Corm refused to speak when Brun asked about the three-stroke sign and split hammer. His hands shook; he touched an old warden-brand scar on his forearm and left to check snares on the ridge. Hild is irritated but says he will talk when he is ready.

Dusk Day 2: Corm arrives alone at the waystation yard, hood up, having followed Brun down from the ridge; he stops at the rope line around the wagon wreck and stares at the chest. He is the hooded patron who paid Ilsa.

Day 3 ~9:20 AM: Brun brought him the ledger and read him the Naming and the captain's note on releasing the sleeper. Corm must choose bind or release, and the keeper's burden. He asks for the day to decide; at dusk he will tell Brun.

Dusk Day 3: Corm decided to release the sleeper with mercy at dawn, not rebind it. He will name the sixty with Brun, rest his hand on the heartstone, and stay at the door as its last keeper until it is done. He asks that Hild be present and that Brun speak Brenn's name last. Garrick met Hild and Corm and stayed to keep the watch at the tunnel mouth.

A small lead-lined chest bound in iron, stamped with the Hearthdeep Wardens' brand, carried hidden in Ilsa's wagon under barrels of lamp oil. Ilsa was paid triple by a stranger (a grey-bearded dwarf with a scarred forearm, hooded, who gave no name) to carry it to the old cairn above the waystation and leave it for collection. It was in the wagon when the slide hit and is still under the wreck. Ilsa does not know what is inside; it is warm to the touch at night and she thinks it hums.

Day 2 afternoon: Brun (Perception 22) watched the wreck from 40 feet. The chest is visible through a split in the false bottom. Rain does not wet the tarp over it: it steams. Faint low hum felt in the teeth. Frost forms on the iron bands though the air is not cold. The slope behind the wreck, where the cairn path meets the road, trickles grit toward it, as if drawn.

Corm's confession (Day 2 dusk): the chest holds the warden's keystone-seal, the 'heartstone' that bound the Iron-Banded Door forty winters ago. Corm, a warden's apprentice, was sworn to keep it; he took it from the door three nights before the slide because he feared Hild's crew would break through and release what the wardens sealed in the lower galleries (a sleeping thing that fouls the air; the 'split hammer' on the map marks its gallery). He meant to hide it in the old warden ward-cairn far from the door but could not carry it far (it burns his scarred arm), so he paid a courier. Removing it weakened the seal: the air seeps, the hill leans toward the stone, the slide followed. The stone wants to return to the door; the longer it is away, the weaker the seal.

The heartstone is back in the Iron-Banded Door but the seal is only half-mended. Brun promised Hild to honor Brenn and the sixty bound dead without opening the door. Needs a true rite of binding, perhaps help from a temple of the Morninglord or Father Dorrin's old knowledge in his prayer book. Corm keeps watch at the door.

Night Day 2: Brun kept vigil with Hild and Corm at the door, reading Father Dorrin's evening prayers in Dwarvish and adding Brenn's name. The stone's breath stayed slow all night. Brun rested there; Day 3 ~6 AM she is rested, with Protection from Evil and Good now prepared.

Day 3 morning: Religion 12 (with Corm, DC 13) just short. Father Dorrin's back pages hold half a rite of binding in his hand, copied from a warden: the opening words and the closing, but the middle ('the Naming') is torn out or missing. Corm says the full rite lives in the wardens' ledger kept in the upper stores of Hearthdeep (the sealed stores where the timbers came from), reachable by a side stair behind the tunnel's first bend. The split hammer on Hild's map marks the sleeper's own gallery, the lowest, where Corm's master walked in. Dorrin's note in the margin: 'Ask Brunhilde's mother's people at the Deepwatch'? (unwritten, hook for later).

Day 3 ~8:50 AM: Brun found the warden-captain's ledger (Investigation nat 20). The Naming recovered: it must be spoken at dawn by a priest of the Morninglord at the Iron-Banded Door while the keeper's hand rests on the heartstone. The ledger also reveals the sleeper was not a monster but something the miners hurt: a mountain's grief, a hollow of old stone-spirit that woke when the lower seam was cut; the wardens bound it out of fear and the Naming can bind OR (with the keeper's consent and the sixty's names read) release it with mercy. Brenn Ironvein is listed as a volunteer who walked in of his own will to keep company with the sleeper and 'hold its hand'. The ledger names the rite's cost: the keeper must stay or be freed by another keeper. Dawn Day 4 is the next rite.

Day 3 ~9:20 AM: Ledger shown to Corm; the choice (bind again or release with mercy) is his as keeper. Brun leaves the decision to him and Hild; dawn Day 4 is the rite. Brun's long rest is due ~6 AM Day 4 and must happen before the rite if she is to have spells.

Dusk Day 3: Corm chose RELEASE with mercy (not rebinding). The rite is at dawn Day 4: names of the sixty, Brenn last, with Brun as the Morninglord's priest and Corm's hand on the stone. Brun should long-rest through the night to have her spells.

Dawn Day 4 (~6 AM): Brun long-rested through the night with Garrick keeping the outer watch and Hild and Corm at the door; all spells restored (3 slots), Channel Divinity ready. Names of the sixty rehearsed aloud before sleep. The rite is about to begin.

Dawn Day 4: the rite succeeded (Insight 17, WIS save 12). The sleeper, a stone-spirit grieving for the lost miners, was named, mourned and released with mercy; the Iron-Banded Door stands open and the lower galleries breathe clean. Hild and Corm will bring up Brenn and the sixty for burial. Brun was marked: a Morninglord's light stood in her holy symbol and the dwarves of the tunnel call her Lantern of Hearthdeep (title). Remaining hook: Father Dorrin's note 'Ask Brunhilde's mother's people at the Deepwatch'.

Sealed warden stores reached by a side stair behind the first bend of Hild's tunnel. Old timbers, tools and records; the wardens' ledger with the Naming is believed to be inside. The stair door is an iron-banded wardens' gate, damp and swollen.

Day 3 ~7 AM: Brun's Athletics (4) and Investigation (1) both failed at the gate. The pry bar slipped and the hinge shrieked; the gate gaped a hand's breadth and a rusted wardens' warning-chime on the lintel (missed by Brun) clanged down the tunnel. Echo carried to the Iron-Banded Door: Corm's voice calls faintly; the seal's hum stirs. Something small and many scuttles inside the stores in the dark.
Day 3 ~7:06 AM: Brun and Hild killed the rat swarm that nested in the stores' threshold. Gate now open; Brun's shield lies on the stair, to be retrieved. The stores beyond are dark and dry-smelling.

Day 3 8:07 AM: Brun and Hild took a short rest at the gate; Corm called that the seal stayed quiet. Brun is at full HP, Channel Divinity restored, one hit die left. Spell slots remain spent (short rest does not restore them) until a long rest (earliest ~6 AM Day 4).
Hild's brother. One of the sixty in the lower galleries of Hearthdeep. The warden ledger records he walked in voluntarily to keep company with the bound sleeper.

Day 4: Found at the head of the sixty, seated against the wall of the lowest gallery, one hand open on his knee as if holding another's. Hild carried him up; he was buried first, with the sixty, in clean earth on the hillside by the old ward-cairn at the waystation's edge.

Title given to Brun by Hild's crew and the dwarves of the cairn after the dawn rite: when she named the sixty and offered mercy, the Morninglord's light stood in her holy symbol and filled the lower gallery. Story only, no mechanical effect.

Hillside field by the old ward-cairn above the Crossroads Waystation where the sixty of Hearthdeep were buried on Day 4 with Brun, Hild, Corm, Garrick and the folk of the waystation. Sixty cairn-stones, one per name.

Old warden stronghold in the high hills north of Hearthdeep, about three days' walk beyond the waystation; the mother-hall of the mine-wardens, where copies of hold ledgers and the names of the lost are kept. Father Dorrin's margin note says Brun's mother's people may be found there. Not yet visited.

Described by Maren on the road: a hall cut into a single mountain, seven galleries high, with a lamp-lit Hall of Names where every warden's death is carved. A few dozen wardens and their kin still live there; it has grown quiet since the holds fell. The captain is Maren's old rival and Brun's great-grandfather's grandnephew, a stern dwarf named Torvald Greycairn (unmet).

Day 6 ~5:30 PM: the party reached the Deepwatch's outer gate ahead of a storm. The gate is a pair of bronze-banded doors set into a sheer cliff under a lamp-lit overhang, with a warden sentry on the wall above who challenges them in Dwarvish and asks the name of Maren's companion.

Father Dorrin's margin note: 'Ask Brunhilde's mother's people at the Deepwatch.' Brun does not remember him ever speaking of it. Hild and Corm say the Deepwatch lies about three days north through the high hills. What Brun knows of her mother is hers to say.

Day 4 ~1 PM: Brun means to pray and tidy Father Dorrin's shrine first, then travel north to the Deepwatch carrying the ledger with Corm's name on it. Hild will send word to the waystation through Garrick if she hears of the wardens' kin.

Day 4 dusk: at Father Dorrin's shrine Brun found a candle lit and the wardens' kin-sign laid on the threshold by Maren Stonehearth, an old warden of the Deepwatch who answers Brun's Dwarvish call from within.

Day 4 evening: Maren told Brun her mother was Sigrun Stonehearth, a warden-surveyor who died shielding her in the shaft collapse. Brun now wears the iron ring with Sigrun's hair. Maren has news from the Deepwatch to share by the fire and wants Brun to come north; the father's name is kept in the Deepwatch records.

Night Day 4: Brun, Maren and Garrick kept the hearth and evening prayers at Father Dorrin's shrine and shared the watch; long rest taken. At dawn Day 5 they set out north for the Deepwatch (about three days) with Maren and Garrick.

Day 5 afternoon: the party (Brun, Garrick, Maren) is on the north road, well into the high hills, making good time under Garrick's guidance. The Deepwatch lies roughly two days further. Next stop: a warden waymark-hut at the saddle for the night.

Day 6 ~6 PM: Brun's Persuasion 20 at the gate: the doors opened. Captain Torvald Greycairn received her in the gate hall, took the ledger to be copied and kept in the Deepwatch archive, and promised her the Hall of Names at first light. Brun and Garrick are guests; Maren has gone to rest.

Day 7 dawn: Torvald took Brun, Maren and Garrick to the Hall of Names. Father: Dagrim Wickwright, lamp-maker, died in the second collapse digging for them. Torvald carved the name himself. Torvald offers Brun a place at the Deepwatch as its priest of the Morninglord, and asks that someone carry the Naming back to other sealed holds; the seal at Hearthdeep proves others may exist. Lead resolved as personal quest; new hook: other sealed holds.

Elderly dwarf woman of the Deepwatch wardens, travel-worn, who lit the candle at Father Dorrin's shrine and left the wardens' kin-sign. She was sent south by the Deepwatch after news of the Hearthdeep seal stirring reached it, and carries a warden's token. Her bond to Brun (what she is to her) is revealed in her own words; she says she knew Brun's mother.

Brun's mother, a warden-surveyor of the Deepwatch who mapped shafts for the hill-holds. Auburn-haired, stubborn-chinned. She died when the shaft she was surveying near the hill-hold collapsed; she shielded her small daughter with her own body, and Brun was found alive beside her days later by Father Dorrin. The iron ring braided with her hair is hers. Brun's father is unnamed so far: Maren says only that he was not a warden and that the rest is for the Deepwatch's records.

Day 5 (Maren's stories on the road): as a girl Sigrun hoarded flat river stones and chalked maps of the Deepwatch's corridors on them; loved barley-and-honey cakes and sour plum jam; sang a work-song about a lamp-maker's daughter, 'Seven Wicks', badly and loudly; refused to wear a helm in the shafts until she cracked her head at twelve. She married outside the wardens (Brun's father) against the captain's wishes.

Night Day 5 at the waymark-hut: Maren taught Brun the words of 'Seven Wicks' and, pressed, gave a little of Brun's father: a hill-hold lamp-maker, a quiet dwarf with soot-black eyes who made lamps for the Deepwatch's seventh gallery and was the reason Sigrun wrote 'Seven Wicks' into every corner; Torvald Greycairn objected because he was not of the wardens and would not swear the oath. His name Maren withholds: it is on the page in the Hall of Names, as the Deepwatch carved it, and she wants Brun to read it there.

Stern, iron-bearded captain of the Deepwatch wardens, Maren's rival of forty years and only friend. Disapproved of Sigrun's marriage to a lamp-maker. Met Brun at the gate hall on Day 6 evening; received the Hearthdeep ledger with solemnity and promised her the Hall of Names at first light.

Brun's father, a quiet hill-hold lamp-maker with soot-dark eyes who made the smokeless lamps of the Deepwatch's seventh gallery and refused the wardens' oath. When the shaft fell on Sigrun and Brun, he dug for them three days with the wardens and died in a second collapse while pulling the last timbers; Dorrin found Brun on the fourth day. Torvald Greycairn had his name cut into the Hall of Names himself in the week after, among the wardens, though he never swore.

Torvald Greycairn says Hearthdeep was not the only hold the wardens sealed in the years the holds fell. Four more seals are named in the Deepwatch archive, their keepers long dead, and the Naming now lets a priest mend or mercifully release them. He asks Brun, the Lantern of Hearthdeep, to consider carrying it. Nearest: Ember Gate, two weeks east.

A single folded leaf pressed flat inside the back cover of Dorrin's prayer book, written in his hand, found by Brun at the Hall of Names on Day 7. It is a letter to Brun: that he kept the book for her, that he wrote three letters to the Deepwatch in her first year, and that he asked them to come and fetch her, never to stay away; that the shaft's second collapse was not as the wardens reported ('the props were cut, child; I have never been sure by whom'); and that she should forgive an old man his silence.

Father Dorrin's last leaf says he sent three letters to the Deepwatch in Brun's first year, asking them to come for her; Maren says only one arrived, and that she was told Brun was safer unknown. He also believed the shaft's props were cut before the second collapse that killed Dagrim, by someone unknown. Someone kept the Deepwatch and Brun apart for forty years.

Day 7: Torvald showed Brun the one letter Maren received, kept in the Deepwatch archive. It is a clean clerk's copy, not Dorrin's cramped hand, sealed with a plain warden's wax stamp. Brun could not tell whose hand wrote it (Investigation 11). Torvald says only the Keeper of the Rolls and the captain's own seal-bearer handled incoming and outgoing post forty years ago; the old Keeper, Osric Vane, still lives in the seventh gallery.

Day 7, Osric Vane (lucid for a while; Brun Insight nat 20): Kell Marrow, Torvald's seal-bearer then, brought him Dorrin's letters already opened, said 'by the captain's word', and told him to burn them and write the one 'safe' reply. Osric could not burn a priest's letters. He hid two of them under a river stone with a chalked corridor (Sigrun's), used as a lid in a lamp-niche on the seventh gallery, and gave them to Brun. The 'captain' then was Haldor Greycairn, Torvald's father. Torvald was truly shocked (Brun's Insight). Kell Marrow died two years after. Who cut the props is still unknown; the letters stopped is now tied to Haldor's order, motive unknown.
Very old dwarf, former Keeper of the Rolls at the Deepwatch, who handled its post forty years ago. Lives in a small cell on the seventh gallery. Possible link to the intercepted letters; unproven.

Torvald Greycairn's father and captain of the Deepwatch forty years ago, now dead. Osric Vane says the seal-bearer Kell Marrow stopped Dorrin's letters 'by the captain's word', so Haldor is the likely source of the order. Unproven; motive unknown.

story.text:
STORY SO FAR (start of game to end of turn 45)

SETTING AND CHARACTER
Brunhilde "Brun" Stonehearth is a Hill Dwarf Life cleric of the Morninglord. She was raised by Father Dorrin Ashbeard, who found her as a starving orphan in a collapsed mine shaft outside a hill-hold. She carries his prayer book. She is optimistic, tries to find common ground, and is suspicious of strangers. She is now level 2 (hit point max 21, AC 18, Channel Divinity once per rest, prepared Healing Word, Guiding Bolt, Sanctuary, Shield of Faith, Protection from Evil and Good; Bless and Cure Wounds always prepared). Her cantrips are Sacred Flame, Guidance and Spare the Dying. The house rules are that a natural 20 on an ability check gives a story bonus, and that level-ups add at least 1 HP.

Day 1, 5:00 PM: Brun arrived at the rain-soaked Crossroads Waystation (a stone inn with a shrine lean-to, on a mountain road). A rockslide had buried a wagon.

THE ROCKSLIDE RESCUE (Day 1)
- Brun rallied the nervous caravan guard, the sullen hunter and the innkeeper (Persuasion 18).
- The hunter is Garrick Thorne: gruff, taciturn, a hunter of twelve winters on these slopes. He advised digging from the left side by the old cairn, which is solid ledge, taking top stones first.
- The trapped were Ilsa (merchant, crushed leg), Tam (mule-driver) and Pip (a small girl).
- Brun read the rubble (Survival 17), dug for about 30 minutes with planks bracing, and freed Pip. She cast Healing Word on Ilsa (7 HP) and levered the cask-rack with Tam (Athletics 16).
- Her first splint failed (Medicine 7). The second try succeeded (Medicine 18), with Cure Wounds (10 HP). XP reached 100.
- Pip gave Brun a small tin bell "for luck". Brun promised to ring it at the end of the story and come back.
- The innkeeper took no coin. Brun long-rested at the waystation.

THE TUNNEL AND THE DWARVES (Day 2)
- Garrick said he had seen lantern light and spoil near the old cairn for two weeks. He read the sawn timbers as hold-wright work.
- Brun failed Perception climbing, and a watcher slipped inside.
- At the tunnel mouth, timbers and a broken pick bore a burned-in brand: a hammer over three wavy lines, the mark of the mine-wardens of Hearthdeep. Hearthdeep is the hold under the hills where Dorrin found Brun (Investigation nat 20).
- Hild Ironvein, a grey-braided dwarf with a crossbow, fired a warning bolt. Brun spoke Dwarvish, left her warhammer at the mouth, and went in alone (Persuasion 12, half-trust). Hild knew "the old Ashbeard". Garrick stayed outside.
- Hild's crew: Aldric (chest crushed by a beam), Dunna (one-eyed, coughing), a young man with a pick (later named Tobin, coughing), and Corm (lean grey-bearded dwarf, a warden's apprentice as a boy, hammer-shaped scar on his left forearm).
- Brun cast Cure Wounds on Aldric (7 HP, Medicine 11). She saw his cough came from foul sweet air seeping from an iron-banded door at the tunnel's end, and got everyone out into the open.
- Hild's reason: forty winters ago the lower galleries fell on half the hold's miners, and the wardens sealed them. Her brother Brenn is among them. She came to bring them out for burial.
- Brun promised to help bring the kin out, but not until the air is understood. Garrick took the sick down to the waystation by cart. XP reached 150.
- Brun could not long-rest again that day, so she had no spells until about 4 AM Day 3.
